Park and Recreation Commission

  Inglewood, California
  March 7, 2023

The Inglewood Park and Recreation Commission meeting was convened in the Council
Chambers located on the ninth floor of City Hall on March 7, 2023. Commissioner Denmon
called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Stephanie Maldonado announced the presence of a quorum as follows:

  Present  Commissioner Lee Denmon - District 1, Octavio Padilla - District 2,
  Cynthia McLemore - District 3, Christopher Beck - District 4
  Absent  Commissioner Henry Brown - Commissioner at Large

City Personnel present for the meeting were as follows:

  Thomas Uwal  Director
  Juan Mata  Park Supervisor
  Bharat Devlia  Human Services Superintendent
  Stephanie Maldonado  Senior Management Assistant
  Anthony Harris  Recreation Supervisor

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None.

MINUTES. None

DIRECTOR’S BUSINESS.

REPORTS - PARKS ADMINISTRATION. Park Supervisor, Juan Mata stated this past month
all Districts were vandalized by graffiti. District 4 was one that was tagged the most in and
around the area of Prairie Avenue from Century Boulevard to Imperial Highway on walls,
poles, and alleyways. Edward Vincent Park was heavily tagged throughout the park in
several restrooms inside and out, poles and the amphitheater walls. The graffiti hotline
is (310) 412-8739.

REPORTS - RECREATION. Recreation Supervisor, Anthony Harris reported the following:
EASTER EGGSTRAVAGANZA: Join the Parks, Recreation and Community Services
Department on Saturday, March 23rd for the 2nd Annual Easter Eggstravaganza. The event
is free and will be held from 11 a.m. to 2 p.m. at Edward Vincent Park. Activities will take
place on the grassy area next to the playhouse. There will be an Easter egg hunt, arts &
crafts, games, magic show and a special visit from the Easter Bunny. We encourage you
to join us for this exciting event! INGLEWOOD STEM FEST: The Department is excited to

  1
   Park and Recreation Commission

host the 3rd Annual Inglewood STEM Fest in partnership with Science of Sport. The event
will be held on Saturday, April 20 from 9:30 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. at Edward Vincent Park. The
free event will expose students in grades Kindergarten through sixth to science,
technology, engineering, and math (STEM) through unique experiences that focus on
several familiar sports. This event is designed to bring in Los Angeles-based sports
organizations to provide an engaging day of STEM and sports to the Inglewood community.
Activity stations will be set-up throughout the event providing STEM lessons centered on
basketball, soccer, tennis, baseball, softball, football, golf, volleyball, and track & field. Last
year’s event was a huge success with over 500 attendees. Community partners for the
event include the Los Angeles Chargers, Los Angeles Dodgers Foundation, Angel City
Football Club, Los Angeles Lakers, Los Angeles Rams, and Los Angeles Clippers to name a
few. Be sure to mark your calendars for this awesome event. IYBL - Inglewood Youth
Basketball League: The City of Inglewood in partnership with the Los Angeles Clippers are
proud to continue our youth basketball league, which benefits the young people of
Inglewood. The league is designed to build the community by introducing the sport of
basketball to children ages 4-14. League goals include fundamental development, skill
progression, team concepts and having fun. Our city staff and volunteer coaches work
together striving to instill important life lessons such as Sportsmanship, Discipline,
Respect, Teamwork, and Perseverance to name a few. In 2024, the league continues to
grow with 352 players, 32 teams, and 21 coaches. Most importantly, we continue to
expand our stand-alone girls’ leagues from one to two offering the Tiny Might Division and
Mighty Might Divisions with girls ages 7-14. Teams practice once a week for one hour at
Rogers or Darby park gymnasiums. Games are currently in the 4th week of league play with
playoffs approaching in early April. The season will conclude by celebrating all 32 teams in
the final week with banquets consisting of food, fun, and awards for all participants. IYSL
– Inglewood Youth Soccer League: The Inglewood Youth Soccer League was introduced in
the winter of 2023 with two divisions and has grown to three divisions in 2024 totaling 133
participants. The league is currently seeking a sponsor but remains strong with 100%
support from the city. Teams practice once a week on Wednesday evenings with games
taking place at Champions Field on Saturday’s from 9:00 am to 1:00 pm. Similar to
basketball, the league will enter playoffs in early April and conclude with the Championship
on Saturday, April 6th. Dodgers Dream Team Baseball – Spring League: Last but not least,
springtime means it is time for Dodger Baseball, Dodgers Dream team baseball that is. The
Dodgers Dream team spring season in Inglewood begins in mid-march and will go through
the month of May. The spring season is designed specifically to focus on the younger age
groups (ages 5-6 T-Ball, 7-8 Coach Pitch). The 5-week season is a developmental
environment that will introduce the game while honing in on the fundamentals of
throwing, catching, hitting, and base running. Teams will practice out of both Darby and
Edward Vincent Jr. parks. The season will consist of nine games in 5 weeks playing under
the lights on Thursday evenings and all day on Saturday’s. The Opening Day ceremony is
scheduled for Saturday April 16th from 10:00 – 11:00 am followed by a full slate of games.

  2
   Park and Recreation Commission

We look forward to the fun. Some of you may be wondering when the older age groups
begin. Registration for the Minors, Majors, Junior Softball, Junior Baseball, Sr. Baseball,
and Sr. Softball begins April 18th with the season set to begin in mid-June. For more
information on our Inglewood Youth Sports Leagues, visit our city sports website at:
https://cityofinglewood.leagueapps.com/

REPORTS - HUMAN SERVICES. Human Services Supervisor, Bharat Devlia reported the
following: Nutrition: We are serving approximately 450 seniors per week through home
delivered meals for homebound seniors and congregate lunches at our Senior Center. We
continue to provide fresh produce weekly in collaboration with the Social Justice Learning
Institute. We are have been working with our seniors to develop new menus for the next
year and are looking forward to many new and exciting additions to our menu, including a
special Juneteenth meal and a Mediterranean salmon lunch. Our next event will be St.
Patrick’s Day featuring a special meal including corn beef, steamed cabbage, boiled new
potatoes, carrot raisin salad, fresh seasonal fruit and a green gelatin dessert. Senior Center
Operation: The senior center continues to thrive. This year has seen some memorable
moments from the Senior Center’s Holiday Christmas Party that provided various forms of
entertainment creating a great atmosphere for our seniors. Seniors truly enjoyed the
Inglewood Inspirational Choir and live eight-piece band called, 8 Piece. Our Valentine’s
Day party saw the lunchroom completely packed with seniors and staff dressed in red and
having fun. We are excited to share that we have a new manager dedicated to the
operations at the Senior Center, Marisela Mansour. Marisela has decades of experience
with the City and has hit the ground running with several new offerings for our seniors,
including presentations from legal nonprofit Bet Tzedek, the USC Leonard Davis School of
Gerontology as well as some very exciting trips and special events that are coming up. Our
Black and White Gala is the first of these exciting new offerings, which will be on March
15, 2024, starting at 5 p.m. at our Inglewood Senior Center. Featuring special guests,
musical performances and hors d’oeuvres, this black tie event is one of three major events
planned for 2024. For tickets, seniors can see the reception at the senior center. Another
very exciting event coordinated by Marisela is our upcoming trip to the opera. A group of
our seniors will be transported to see Giuseppe Verdi’s La Traviata on Thursday, April 4,
2024, at 2:00 PM. A packed lunch will be provided, and this wonderful production includes
a performance of Brindisi, a song most of us know by sound, if not by name. Senior
Transportation: Our paratransit program continues to provide trips to seniors in and
around the cities of Inglewood and Hawthorne. Our taxi program since transitioning to
the Taxi Card has been doing quite well with minimal to no complaints reported. There is
a new transportation service for those who are disabled called Butterfli. This new free
service is a pilot program provided by Metro and provides transportation service within a
12-mile radius from the rider’s pick up point. Some seniors have been taking advantage of
this new service. Finally, one of our fellow bus operators James Ellis retired at the start of
January 2024, after serving for nearly two decades. We want to wish him well in his

  3
   Park and Recreation Commission

retirement and to thank him for his service. CACFP: The Child and Adult Care Food Program
(CACFP) serves meals to youth 18 years old and under and operates at Crenshaw Library,
Inglewood Main Library, Rogers Park, and Darby Park . The program's hours are Monday
through Friday, providing supper from 2:30 PM - 3:30 PM and snack from 4:30 PM - 5:00
PM. We continue to serve an average of 115 suppers and 50 snacks per week.

REPORTS - DIRECTOR. Director, Thomas Uwal reported on the following: Community
Information Guide (CIG) Spring/Summer Edition 2024: Staff will be assisting the Director
with the upcoming guide that should be complete by May 1st. Park Project Updates:
Vincent Park Restroom Project Phase 2 was completed in November 2023. Darby Park
Walking Track Replacement Project was completed in March 2024 and looks great. Darby
Park Restroom Project has been completed. Commissioner Information: Ethics Refresher
Training is now due, a link will be sent out via email for completion.

PUBLIC COMMENTS. None

COMMISSIONER COMMENTS. Commissioner Padilla invited everyone to attend the
Inglewood Little League opening day on Saturday at Rogers Park.

There being no further business to be presented, Commissioner Denmon declared the
meeting adjourned at the hour of 6:30 p.m.
